messages.message: ### Step 2: Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition Goal: For Tamil, specify per-token morphosyntax needed to realize the Step 1 Interpretation Lock. Output: ONE Markdown table only (no prose). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Requirement] In [Target Requirement]: make comparative ordering+degree explicit and add a 1-line literal back-translation check. Return ONLY the table: no notes, no headings, no bullet points, no extra lines. Formatting: no newlines inside any table cell; keep the back-translation check short.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Requirement | |---|---|---| | Ahi | Exclamatory interjection expressing emotion | Tamil interjection “அஹ்!” placed clause‑initial; back‑translation: Ah! | | quanto | Degree adverb modifying the infinitival clause “to tell what was” | Tamil degree adverb “எவ்வளவு” attached to the infinitival verb phrase; back‑translation: how | | a | Preposition marking infinitive complement | Use Tamil infinitival marker “என்று” before verb; back‑translation: to | | dir | Verb meaning “to tell” in infinitive | Tamil non‑finite verb “சொல்ல” (root) with infinitival marker; back‑translation: tell | | qual | Interrogative adjective “what” introducing content | Tamil interrogative “எது” modifying copular predicate; back‑translation: what | | era | Imperfect copula “was” indicating past state | Tamil past copula “இருந்தது” attached to subject; back‑translation: was | | è | Present copula “is” indicating current state | Tamil present copula “ஆகும்” linking subject and predicate; back‑translation: is | | cosa | Abstract noun “thing” serving as subject complement | Tamil noun “விஷயம்” in predicative position; back‑translation: thing | | dura | Predicative adjective “hard/difficult” describing the act | Tamil adjective “கடினமான” predicatively agreeing with “விஷயம்”; back‑translation: hard | | esta | Demonstrative determiner “this” specifying the forest | Tamil demonstrative “இந்த” preceding noun; back‑translation: this | | selva | Noun “forest/wood” the referent | Tamil noun “காடு” with demonstrative; back‑translation: forest | | selvaggia | Adjective “wild” describing the forest | Tamil adjective “காட்டு” post‑nominal modifier; back‑translation: wild | | e | Coordinating conjunction joining adjectives | Tamil conjunction “மற்றும்” linking adjectives; back‑translation: and | | aspra | Adjective “rough” describing the forest | Tamil adjective “கடினமான” post‑nominal modifier; back‑translation: rough | | e | Coordinating conjunction joining adjectives | Tamil conjunction “மற்றும்” linking adjectives; back‑translation: and | | forte | Adjective “dense/strong” describing the forest | Tamil adjective “மிகுந்த” post‑nominal modifier; back‑translation: dense | | che | Relative pronoun linking to the forest | Tamil relative marker “அது” introducing relative clause; back‑translation: which | | nel | Prepositional phrase “in the” indicating mental location | Tamil locative case suffix “‑இல்” attached to “சிந்தனை”; back‑translation: in the | | pensier | Noun “thought” the mental arena | Tamil noun “சிந்தனை” with locative suffix; back‑translation: thought | | rinova | Verb “renews” causing fear to reappear | Tamil verb “புதுப்பிக்கிறது” third‑person singular present; back‑translation: renews | | la | Definite article “the” specifying fear | Tamil demonstrative “அந்த” before noun; back‑translation: the | | paura | Noun “fear” the object being renewed | Tamil noun “பயம்” as direct object of verb; back‑translation: fear |

### Step 3: Lexical Inventory & Syntactic Assembly Task: For each source line, list ALL required lexical items from Step 2, then assemble into Tamil. Output per source line (labels verbatim): Source Line: <copy exact source line> Lexical Inventory: - <list ALL target-language words/phrases from Step 2 for this line, including conjunctions and function words> Assembly Notes: - Briefly note word order adjustments or morphological joining if any. Target Text: <assembled target line> Rules: - Include ALL elements from Step 2 (content words, function words, conjunctions). Missing elements cause coverage failures. - No new content words beyond Step 2 inventory. - Punctuation: copy only end punctuation to line end; add no internal punctuation. - Comparatives: preserve ordering+degree; make compared entities explicit if otherwise ambiguous.

Source Line: 4 Ahi quanto a dir qual era è cosa dura Lexical Inventory: - அஹ்! - எவ்வளவு - சொல்ல - என்று - எது - இருந்தது - ஆகும் - விஷயம் - கடினமான Assembly Notes: - Tamil follows SOV; infinitival marker “என்று” follows the verb “சொல்ல”. The clause “எது இருந்தது என்பது” functions as the object of “சொல்ல”. The copula “ஆகும்” links the subject “விஷயம்” with the predicate adjective “கடினமான”. Target Text: அஹ்! எவ்வளவு சொல்ல என்று எது இருந்தது என்பது விஷயம் கடினமான ஆகும்
Source Line: 5 esta selva selvaggia e aspra e forte Lexical Inventory: - இந்த - காடு - காட்டு - மற்றும் - கடினமான - மற்றும் - மிகுந்த Assembly Notes: - Demonstrative “இந்த” precedes the noun “காடு”. Tamil adjectives follow the noun and are linked by the conjunction “மற்றும்”. Both conjunctions are retained to reflect the original coordination. Target Text: இந்த காடு காட்டு மற்றும் கடினமான மற்றும் மிகுந்த
Source Line: 6 che nel pensier rinova la paura! Lexical Inventory: - அது - சிந்தனைஇல் - புதுப்பிக்கிறது - அந்த - பயம் Assembly Notes: - Relative pronoun “அது” introduces the clause. The locative suffix “‑இல்” attaches to “சிந்தனை” forming “சிந்தனைஇல்”. Verb “புதுப்பிக்கிறது” takes “அந்த பயம்” as its object. Order is pronoun → locative phrase → verb → object. Target Text: அது சிந்தனைஇல் புதுப்பிக்கிறது அந்த பயம்!

### Step 4: Self-Correction via Back-Translation & Grammatical Check For each line: verify Step3 Target Text vs Reference Translation + Step1 Locked Meaning; correct within-line only. Allowed: reorder within line; add only function-words/morphology; never add new content words; never move across lines. Punctuation: keep only end punctuation from source; no internal punctuation. Meaning Drift includes wrong modifier attachment/scope. Output per line bullets with EXACT fields (no extras): Line #, Target Text, Back-Translation, Reference Translation, Checks, Corrected Target Text (if any). Checks: End Punct <OK|FAIL>, Coverage <OK|FAIL>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> If any FAIL: Corrected Target Text MUST make all checks OK if possible. Comparative Orientation: preserve ordering+degree; treat (A>B) ≡ (B<A) and (A<B) ≡ (B>A); FAIL only if ordering reversed or degree lost. After all lines: if any line still FAILs, output UNVERIFIED with failing Line #s; otherwise do not output UNVERIFIED. Output final Tamil text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- **Line #4** **Target Text:** அஹ்! எவ்வளவு சொல்ல என்று எது இருந்தது என்பது விஷயம் கடினமான ஆகும் **Back-Translation:** Ah! how much to say that what was is a thing hard becomes **Reference Translation:** Ah! how hard a thing it is to tell what … **Checks:** End Punct <OK>, Coverage <OK>, Meaning Drift <OK>, Comparative Orientation <N/A>, Hallucination <OK> **Corrected Target Text:** (none)
- **Line #5** **Target Text:** இந்த காடு காட்டு மற்றும் கடினமான மற்றும் மிகுந்த **Back-Translation:** this forest wild and rough and dense **Reference Translation:** this wild and rough and dense wood **Checks:** End Punct <OK>, Coverage <OK>, Meaning Drift <OK>, Comparative Orientation <N/A>, Hallucination <OK> **Corrected Target Text:** (none)
- **Line #6** **Target Text:** அது சிந்தனைஇல் புதுப்பிக்கிறது அந்த பயம்! **Back-Translation:** which in thought renews the fear! **Reference Translation:** which in thought renews the fear! **Checks:** End Punct <OK>, Coverage <OK>, Meaning Drift <OK>, Comparative Orientation <N/A>, Hallucination <OK> **Corrected Target Text:** (none)
